mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances with declining HOUST, or correlation between HOUST and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5pp does not correlate with subsequent negative S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances with increasing INDPRO, or correlation between INDPRO and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) shows annualized growth below 2%, this combination signals a potential monetary policy misalignment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not significantly predict S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 over the past month, combined with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points, signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between PAYEMS and UNRATE does not significantly predict S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances with increasing RSAFS, or correlation between RSAFS and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.25 percentage points in a month, and the GDP (GDPC1) shows a quarterly growth rate below 2%, this combination signals a potential economic slowdown despite easing monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 does not significantly predict S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05).
